newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond players say more supply on horizon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond players say more supply on horizon.

text.p: Oportunistic borrowers continue to tap the corporate bond primary market at a heated pace as U.S. Treasury yields remain at their lowest levels since the spring, dealers said.
"There's more debt on the horizon," said one syndicate source. "Expect about another billion in new debt today."
As another chunk of debt gets set to hit the new issue arena, players caution that the market may be in for some supply indigestion after Wednesday's total of about $1.5 billion in new straight debt.
"The market may suffer from a little indigestion with the bulk of new supply out there," said one syndicate source.
Investment grade issuance made up the bulk of Wednesday's supply with a little over $1.0 billion priced as issuers rushed to get their financing needs met at less costly levels, dealers added.
On Thursday, Norwest Financial priced $150 million in five-year notes to yield 27 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Apache Corp priced $150 milllion in 100-year Baa1/BBB rated debt to yield 95 basis points via Goldman Sachs.
Among other deals expected to come to market on Thursday are Tribune Corp's $250 million of A3/A-rated 10-year debt via Merrill Lynch.
McDonnell Douglas is expected to issue $200 million of 10-year debt, also via Merrill Lynch.
In private placement deals, Levi Strauss is expected to price a two-part 144A debt offering consisting of $350 million in seven-year debt and $450 million in 10-year debt, via Goldman Sachs.
Dealers said Banque Nationale de Paris's planned debt offering had been postponed following rumors that the bank was in the midst of making an acquisition.
"BNP's deal has been postponed," said one dealer. "The bank may be in the process of buying a company, so the deal may be on hold for a while."
Dealers said most of Wednesday's deals went well but that Ford Motor Co's $500 million 50-year bond deal was priced at a tight level.
"Some deals met with good demand but the Ford deal was priced tight," said a syndicate source.
Ford's 7.40 percent 50-year bonds, which initally priced at a spread of 77 basis points, were seen trading in the secondary market at 83 basis points bid, 79 offered, traders said.
Praxair's new 6.90 percent 10-year debt, priced at a spread of 52 basis points, traded up to 59 bid, 57 offered, they said.
May Department Stores's 6.875 percent nine-year notes were seen trading at 52 bid, 49 offered, after pricing at a spread of 51 basis points.
In the government market, the 30-year bond was up 9/32 at 100-27/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
